Consider the circle of radius $6$ centered at $(-5,-2)$, as shown above. Construct a set of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ that traverse the circle once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A(1,-2).$

$x=$
{{field-1}}$,\,y=$
{{field-2}}$,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi )$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a circle of radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ are

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +a,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +b,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the circle is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(r+a,b).$

In our case, we have a circle of radius $6$ centered at the point $(-5,-2).$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the circle are

$$
x=6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -5,\,y=6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -2,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
